sentences.text: Researchers used a mouse model of depression induced by corticosterone and hippocampal neuron cultures to investigate the relationship between the proteins XBP-1s and EAAT2. They measured behavioral changes, cell damage, and synaptic and mitochondrial function, finding that corticosterone treatment increased XBP-1s levels while decreasing EAAT2, which coincided with rising glutamate in the hippocampus.

Lowering XBP-1 levels in cells restored normal EAAT2 expression and reduced excess glutamate and oxidative stress. In the animal model, administering Toyocamycin lessened depression-like symptoms and brain cell damage, matching lower XBP-1s and higher EAAT2 levels, suggesting XBP-1 signaling activity is functionally linked to EAAT2 expression in these setups.

The authors conclude that it remains unknown whether EAAT2 is the specific reason why lowering XBP-1 protects neurons, noting that these findings apply only to the specific experimental conditions tested.
